solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American, back across Atlantic, passes over money in Chicago

indicators.note: across says the reversed letters are stretched over either side of the ocean's nickname
back says the short word for American is turned round

parts.note: the Pond is the jocular name for the Atlantic
licks means passes the tongue over

explanation.surface: A transatlantic traveller hands over cash in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the American abbreviation round, and 'across' has it straddle the ocean's nickname. 'in Chicago' marks the money slang as American.
explanation.definitionFit: This is old American slang for cash, so it is fairly flagged as Chicago usage.

clue.text: Man's a favourite with the Queen

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: Some fellow is a royal favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so an example of a man.

clue.text: Gathers stringed instrument is a Japanese speciality

parts.note: nets means gathers in, as with a catch
uke is short for ukulele

explanation.surface: Collecting a ukulele-type instrument is something Japan specialises in.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved toggle for a kimono sash, a distinctly Japanese craft item.

clue.text: A lot of relative notice is uncovered

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the relative loses its final letter

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
an ad is a notice, an advertisement

explanation.surface: Much of a family member's announcement has been exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without clothes is being bare or naked, i.e. uncovered.

clue.text: Ate half of orange in various diets

indicators.note: in says one piece sits within the other
various says the letters of diets are rearranged
half of takes the back three letters of orange

explanation.surface: Someone ate part of an orange on a succession of diets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' turns DIETS into ISTED, and NGE, the latter half of orange, goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest food is to take it in by swallowing, i.e. to eat it.

clue.text: Unexpectedly take in Rossini's initial material for horn?

indicators.note: unexpectedly says the letters turn up in a surprising order
initial picks the first letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: Absorbing the start of a Rossini piece written for the horn, against expectation.
explanation.walkthrough: TAKEIN plus R is rearranged. The '?' marks that horn is the animal substance, not the instrument the musical surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous protein makes up animal horns, hooves, hair and nails.

clue.text: Motoring offence evident in Tipperary?

parts.note: the place name has a P twice over, so it shows a 'double P', followed in the pun by leaving a car alongside another

explanation.surface: A traffic violation spotted in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: Tipperary, an Irish county, is spelt with two Ps side by side: a double P, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving a car alongside one already parked at the kerb is a traffic offence.

clue.text: Insect cracking open country banana

indicators.note: cracking open says the insect breaks into the countryside word

parts.note: plain is flat open country
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug breaks open a banana from the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open' looks like part of 'open country' but belongs with 'cracking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy cooking banana, so a kind of banana.

clue.text: Know drink will lead to one episode involving introduction of carnal desire

parts.note: con is an archaic verb meaning to know or study
a cup is a drink, as in a fruit cup
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: involving says the episode word takes in another letter

parts.note: a scene is an episode

indicators.note: introduction of takes the opening letter of carnal

explanation.surface: Knowing that drinking leads to an episode with a carnal angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will lead to' just orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is lust or strong sexual longing, a kind of desire.

clue.text: Chamber work? Recalled some Schubert etc. obviously

indicators.note: Recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Recalling a chamber piece by Schubert and others.
explanation.walkthrough: TETCO sits inside 'etc. obviously' and 'Recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece for eight players, as in Schubert's famous one, is a chamber composition.

clue.text: Blend of garlic oil used in smoking?

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so these letters are combined anew

explanation.surface: A garlic-oil mixture used for smoking food.
explanation.walkthrough: Smoking suggests the kitchen; the '?' points to tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thin cigar, an item people smoke.

clue.text: 'English marines brought in germ,' answer islanders

indicators.note: brought in says these letters are placed within the others

parts.note: a bud is a germ, the first growth
RM stands for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: Islanders respond that the marines brought an infection with them.
explanation.walkthrough: Germ means an infection on the surface but a bud in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of an Atlantic British territory are islanders.

clue.text: Medicine that's almost extremely pleasant? Almost

indicators.note: almost says the word for extremely is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: too means extremely

indicators.note: Almost says the word for pleasant loses its tail

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: Medicine that is nearly too nice to take.
explanation.definitionFit: A restorative drink or remedy, so a medicine.

clue.text: Prints from this artist are expensive in Paris

parts.note: es is French for 'are', as in tu es; 'in Paris' covers it too
cher is French for expensive

explanation.surface: This artist's prints fetch high prices in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' makes both words French. 'Prints from' just leads in.
explanation.definitionFit: M. C. Escher was a Dutch graphic artist known for impossible-looking prints.

clue.text: Reduced time filling container with grain

indicators.note: filling says the time letter goes inside the container

parts.note: a cup is a container
rice is a grain

explanation.surface: Cutting time spent filling a container with grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Sold at a lowered rate, so reduced in price.

clue.text: One rigged new line with quantity of current for light

indicators.note: rigged means fixed or manipulated, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an amp is a unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Someone rigged a new cable with a dose of current to make a light.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas discharge lamp glowing red, a source of light.

clue.text: Ignoring what composer may be doing about note

indicators.note: about says the composer's activity goes around the note letter

parts.note: scoring is writing music for instruments

explanation.surface: A composer is ignoring a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating with contempt and dismissing is a way of pointedly ignoring.

clue.text: Arab diplomacy securing English and French object?

parts.note: AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

indicators.note: securing says the diplomacy word holds the two letters inside it

parts.note: tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: Arab diplomacy wins over the English and French: what is the aim?
explanation.walkthrough: Object looks like a goal; it is a made thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-made item, especially of historical interest, is an object.

clue.text: Ruffian vandalised entertainment centre

indicators.note: vandalised means smashed up, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A thug wrecked an amusement venue.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling fair with rides and stalls is a place for entertainment.

clue.text: Attractive man's affair recalled lust, perhaps

parts.note: ado is a fuss or affair, a to-do

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the sin is read backwards

parts.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A handsome man's affair brought back memories of lust.
explanation.definitionFit: The beautiful youth loved by Venus in myth, used for any handsome man.

clue.text: Dee's a river? Just a trickle

parts.note: dee is the letter D spelt out
the Ribble is a river in Lancashire, northern England

explanation.surface: The River Dee barely flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dee looks like the Welsh river, but is only the letter's name; the Ribble is the river, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin small flow of liquid is a trickle.

clue.text: Sent as soldiers, though lacking power to capture Northern port

indicators.note: to capture says the shortened word takes the extra letter inside
lacking says the letter for power is left out

parts.note: soldiers are posted to a station, i.e. sent there

explanation.surface: Troops dispatched, though underpowered, to seize a northern harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping P leaves OSTED, which takes N.
explanation.definitionFit: A Belgian ferry port on the North Sea coast.

clue.text: Amount one knows about Arkansas girl

indicators.note: about says the knowledge word goes round the state code

parts.note: ken is range of knowledge
AR is the postal code for Arkansas

explanation.surface: How much someone knows about a girl from Arkansas.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Decay that is enveloping whip to punish student

parts.note: rust is decay of metal

indicators.note: enveloping says the abbreviation wraps round the whip

parts.note: ie is id est, that is
a cat (o' nine tails) is a whip

explanation.surface: A rotting whip used to discipline a student.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and Cambridge, to send a student down temporarily as a penalty.

clue.text: Article is briefly snatched by man — that's a crime

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: snatched by says the short form is grabbed inside the name

parts.note: Ron is a man's name
is shortened becomes 's, as in it's

explanation.surface: Someone grabbed an article, which is a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a crime.

clue.text: Muses, perhaps, about broken crate for fruit

indicators.note: about says the number word goes around the other letters

parts.note: the Muses were nine in number

indicators.note: broken says the letters of crate are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pondering a smashed crate of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Muses looks like a verb; it means the nine goddesses. 'broken' turns CRATE into ECTAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned peach variety, a fruit.

clue.text: Fundamental book, one faithfully reproduced

parts.note: a means one
sic marks text reproduced exactly as written

explanation.surface: An essential book, copied exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary or essential, i.e. fundamental.

clue.text: Actress showing deep emotions generated in plays

indicators.note: plays means moves freely about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actress conveying powerful feelings in theatre roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays' looks like drama but signals the anagram; 'in' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A female performer specialising in serious drama roles is an actress of deep emotion.
